core_obligations: Reduce part (1) to part (2): centrality of the Chern classes in the bivariant theory is an immediate consequence of the commutation statement (proof line 7602).

Compute the relation after applying a bivariant class: write the classes obtained by capping the given class with the Chern classes of the bundle, record their characterising relation on the projective bundle of the bundle, apply the bivariant class to that relation, and use centrality of the first Chern class together with the properties of bivariant classes to rewrite the result as the same relation on the base changed projective bundle, with the author omitting the calculation (proof lines 7603-7624).

Conclude by uniqueness: the characterisation of the Chern classes identifies the classes thus obtained with the caps of the Chern classes of the pulled back bundle applied to the image of the original class, which is the commutation statement, and the last assertion on two commuting caps is a special case (proof lines 7625-7628).
proof_roadmap: Apply the bivariant class to the characterising relation (proof lines 7603-7624).
Identify the result by uniqueness and read off the commutation (proof lines 7625-7628).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the Chern classes of a locally free module are central in the bivariant theory and commute with arbitrary bivariant classes, with the consequence that capping with the Chern classes of two bundles commutes (statement lines 7580-7599, tag 0F9A-adjacent). The proof records the characterising relation for the classes obtained by capping with the Chern classes, applies the bivariant class to that relation, uses centrality of the first Chern class and the bivariant axioms to move it past the cap and the flat pullback, and then identifies the result by the uniqueness in the characterisation. That manipulation is the substance, so the claim is H2.
